title: Global Warming & Cleaner Fuels
description: The final showdown! Choose cleaner fuels, cool the planet, and relight the Guardian Flame to defeat Lord Cinder for good.

content.value: When we burn fuels, we release carbon dioxide (CO₂). CO₂ traps heat from the Sun in the atmosphere, like a blanket around the Earth. As CO₂ levels rise, the whole planet slowly heats up — this is GLOBAL WARMING.
Global warming is causing serious changes: melting polar ice, rising sea levels, more extreme weather, and threats to plants, animals and people. Reducing how much fuel we burn helps slow it down.

MORE CO₂  →  more heat trapped  →  Earth warms up
🏭 burning fuels → 💨 CO₂ rises → 🌡️ temperatures climb
→ 🧊 melting ice, 🌊 rising seas, ⛈️ extreme weather

We can fight global warming by using cleaner fuels and less of them: switch to gaseous fuels like CNG and LPG, use hydrogen and renewable energy (solar, wind), plant more trees to absorb CO₂, and save energy by walking, cycling and sharing transport.
Every bit of fuel saved means less CO₂. Planting trees, using CNG/solar power, and saving electricity all help cool the planet — small actions add up.

Key Takeaway: Burning fuels releases CO₂, which traps heat and causes global warming — melting ice, rising seas and extreme weather. Using cleaner fuels, renewable energy and planting trees helps reduce it.

quiz.question: Global warming is mainly caused by rising levels of…
options: carbon dioxide trapping heat in the atmosphere
quiz.explain: Extra CO₂ from burning fuels traps the Sun's heat, warming the whole planet.

quiz.question: Which is a way to reduce global warming?
options: using cleaner fuels and planting trees
quiz.explain: Cleaner fuels, renewable energy and more trees all reduce CO₂ and slow global warming.

quiz.question: One effect of global warming is…
options: melting polar ice and rising sea levels
quiz.explain: Global warming melts polar ice and raises sea levels, among other serious effects.
